tables.description: Summary statistics: annualized mean return and volatility of each futures contract, 1965-2009.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct data ingestion and instrument mapping (58 liquid futures mapped to Datastream continuous calc series per Appendix A exchanges), correct daily-to-monthly compounding of excess returns, and the annualization conventions (arithmetic mean x12, std x sqrt(12)). Matching per-instrument means and volatilities validates the universe, contract selection, roll handling, and the excess-return definition before any strategy code runs.
tables.paper_quote: Summary statistics on futures contracts. Reported are the annualized mean return and volatility (standard deviation) of the futures contracts in our sample from January 1965 to December 2009 as well as the mean and standard deviation of the Net speculator long positions in each contract as a percentage of open interest, covered and defined by the CFTC data, which are available over the period January 1986 to December 2009. For a detailed description of our sample of futures contracts, see Appendix A.
tables.notes: 53 of 58 instruments: the last currency rows (CHF/USD truncated mid-cell plus the 4 rows after it) were lost in OCR parsing. CFTC Net speculator position columns (paper cols 3-4) are excluded from this run — positions analysis is deferred (see REPORT.md scope). Pre-futures index splices (MSCI country / JPM bond indexes before futures listing) are not available in ClickHouse; series start at futures availability, documented in assumptions.md.

tables.description: t-statistics of alphas of time series momentum strategies across look-back (k) and holding (h) periods, by asset class.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct TSMOM strategy construction — sign-of-past-return signal, 1/sigma ex ante volatility position sizing, Jegadeesh-Titman overlapping-cohort aggregation for h>1 — and the 7-factor alpha regression methodology, across the full k x h horizon grid. The signature pattern (strong positive t-stats for k<=12, decay and reversal at k=24-48) validates the signal timing and holding-period mechanics simultaneously for all assets and for commodities, equity indexes, and bonds separately.
tables.paper_quote: Reported are the $t$ -statistics of the alphas (intercepts) from time series regressions of the returns of time series momentum strategies over various look-back and holding periods on the following factor portfolios: MSCI World Index, Lehman Brothers/Barclays Bond Index, S&P GSCI Index, and HML, SMB, and UMD Fama and French factors from Ken French’s Web site. Panel A reports results for all asset classes, Panel B for commodity futures, Panel C for equity index futures, Panel D for bond futures, and Panel E for currency forwards.
tables.notes: Panel A (all assets), B (commodities), C (equity indexes) complete; Panel D (bonds) k=1..12 only (k=24/36/48 rows and Panel E currencies were OCR-truncated). MKT/BOND/GSCI passives are proxied by equal-weighted portfolios of the paper's own equity-index/bond/commodity futures (MSCI World, Barclays Aggregate, S&P GSCI are not in ClickHouse); SMB/HML/UMD are exact from ff.four_factor_monthly. Paper betas on the three passive indexes are small (|beta|<=0.11), so intercept impact is expected small.

tables.description: Time series regressions of the diversified TSMOM factor on MSCI World and Fama-French SMB, HML, UMD, monthly and quarterly non-overlapping.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct construction of the diversified TSMOM FACTOR itself (40% ex ante volatility targeting per instrument, equal-weighting across the S_t available instruments, k=12/h=1) — the paper's headline asset — and the factor-model regression methodology (monthly plus quarterly non-overlapping). The headline alpha of 1.58%/month with a small UMD loading is the paper's central abnormal-return claim.
tables.paper_quote: Panel A reports results from time series regressions of monthly and non-overlapping quarterly returns on the diversified time series momentum strategy that takes an equal-weighted average of the time series momentum strategies across all futures contracts in all asset classes, on the returns of the MSCI World Index and the Fama and French factors SMB, HML, and UMD, representing the size, value, and cross-sectional momentum premiums in US stocks. Panel B reports results using the Asness, Moskowitz, and Pedersen (2010) value and momentum “everywhere” factors instead of the Fama and French factors, which capture the premiums to value and cross-sectional momentum globally across asset classes. Panel C reports results from regressions of the time series momentum returns on the market (MSCI World Index), volatility (VIX), funding liquidity (TED spread), and sentiment variables from Baker and Wurgler (2006, 2007), as well as their extremes.
tables.notes: MSCI World (the market regressor) is proxied by the equal-weighted portfolio of the paper's 9 equity index futures; SMB/HML/UMD are exact from ff.four_factor_monthly. Panels B (AMP 2010 everywhere factors) and C (VIX/TED/sentiment) are out of scope: those factor data are not in ClickHouse.

tables.description: Correlations of TSMOM strategy returns and passive long positions, within and across asset classes.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that per-instrument TSMOM return series and the passive-long comparison series are correctly constructed at the instrument level (not just the diversified factor), and that asset-class aggregation is correct. The paper's distinctive claim — TSMOM correlations ACROSS asset classes exceed passive-long correlations across classes — is a pattern-level check on the cross-asset dependence structure that no other selected table exercises.
tables.paper_quote: Panel A reports within each asset class the average pair-wise correlation of each instruments’ 12-month time series momentum strategy returns, as well as a passive long position in each instrument. Panel B reports the correlation of time series momentum strategies and passive long positions across asset classes, where an equal-weighted average of the instruments within each asset class is first formed and then the correlations between the equal-weighted strategies across asset classes are calculated. Correlations are calculated from monthly returns over the period January 1985–December 2009.

tables.description: Regressions of XSMOM strategies (all assets and by asset class), Fama-French UMD/HML/SMB on the TSMOM factor.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct cross-sectional momentum construction (rank-relative-to-median weights on 12-month returns with the most recent month skipped, volatility-scaled like TSMOM) and validates the TSMOM-vs-XSMOM relationship: TSMOM's near-complete explanation of XSMOM (alpha approx 0 for all, COM, FI, FX) and of UMD (loading 0.49, alpha -0.28%, t=-0.93) is the paper's Section 5 claim that time series momentum subsumes cross-sectional momentum premiums.
tables.paper_quote: Panel A reports results from regressions of the 12-month time series momentum strategies by asset class (TSMOM) on 12-month cross-sectional momentum strategies (XSMOM) of Asness, Moskowitz, and Pedersen (2010). Panel B reports results from the decomposition of cross-sectional momentum and time series momentum strategies according to Section 4.2, where Auto is the component of profits coming from the auto-covariance of returns, Cross is the component coming from cross-serial correlations or lead-lag effects across the asset returns, Mean is the component coming from cross-sectional variation in unconditional mean returns, and Mean squared is the component coming from squared mean returns. Panel C reports results from regressions of several XSMOM strategies in different asset classes, the Fama-French momentum, value, and size factors, and two hedge fund indexes obtained from Dow Jones/Credit Suisse on our benchmark TSMOM factor.
tables.notes: Last two rows of Panel C (Dow Jones/Credit Suisse Managed Futures and Global Macro hedge fund indexes) excluded — index data not in ClickHouse. XSMOM US stocks row (Panel A only) not in Panel C.
